title: Sum of evens
prompt:
Write `sum_of_evens(numbers)` that returns the sum of the even integers in the list.
Return 0 when there are none.
hints: Loop over the numbers and keep a running total.
A number is even when `n % 2 == 0`. Negative numbers follow the same rule.
Start with `total = 0`, add `n` inside `if n % 2 == 0:`, and `return total` after the loop.

title: FizzBuzz
prompt:
Write `fizzbuzz(n)` that returns a list of strings for the numbers 1 to n.
Use `"Fizz"` for multiples of 3, `"Buzz"` for multiples of 5, `"FizzBuzz"` for both, and the number as a string otherwise.
Return an empty list when n is 0.
hints: Use a `for` loop over `range(1, n + 1)` and build a result list.
Check divisibility by both 3 and 5 first. If you check 3 first, 15 will be labelled "Fizz".
When no rule matches, append `str(i)`.

title: Word count
prompt:
Write `word_count(text)` that returns a dictionary mapping each word to how many times it appears.
Words are separated by whitespace and counting ignores case, so `"The the"` gives `{"the": 2}`.
Punctuation is not special: treat it as part of the word.
hints: A dictionary maps each word to its count.
`text.lower().split()` gives lowercase words and copes with repeated spaces.
For each word use `counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1`.

title: Squares of odd numbers
prompt:
Write `squares_of_odds(numbers)` that returns a list with the square of every odd number, in the original order.
Try to do it with a list comprehension.
hints: A list comprehension looks like `[expression for item in items if condition]`.
An odd number has `n % 2 == 1` (this also works for negative numbers in Python).
The expression you want to keep is `n * n`.

title: Safe integer parsing
prompt:
Write `parse_int(value)` that returns `int(value)`, or `None` if the value cannot be converted.
It must not raise: handle both bad text and values of the wrong type.
hints: Wrap the conversion in `try` and handle the failure in `except`.
`int('abc')` raises ValueError and `int(None)` raises TypeError. Catch both with `except (ValueError, TypeError):`.
Return `int(value)` inside `try`, and `None` inside the `except` block.

title: Make a URL slug
prompt:
Write `slugify(title)` that turns a title into a URL slug.
Lowercase the text, replace every run of characters that are not letters or digits with a single hyphen, and remove hyphens from both ends.
hints: Process the text one character at a time, or use the `re` module.
`re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', text)` replaces each run of other characters with one hyphen (remember `import re`).
Lowercase first, then use `.strip('-')` to remove hyphens at the ends.

title: Classify an HTTP status code
prompt: Write `status_category(code)` that returns the class of an HTTP status code: `"informational"` (100-199), `"success"` (200-299), `"redirect"` (300-399), `"client error"` (400-499), `"server error"` (500-599), or `"unknown"` for anything else.
hints: Compare the code against ranges, for example `200 <= code < 300`.
Check each range with `if` / `elif`, and finish with an `else` that returns "unknown".
Integer division helps too: `code // 100` is 2 for every 2xx code.

title: Parse a query string
prompt:
Write `parse_query_string(query)` that turns `"a=1&b=2"` into `{"a": "1", "b": "2"}`.
Rules: an empty string gives `{}`; empty parts are skipped; a key without `=` gets the value `""`; only the first `=` splits (so `token=abc==` keeps `abc==`); a repeated key keeps its last value.
hints: Split the string on `&` first, then split each part into a key and a value.
Use `part.split('=', 1)` so a value containing `=` stays in one piece, and skip empty parts.
If a part has no `=`, use an empty string as the value. Assigning to the same key again overrides the old value.

title: Mean squared error
prompt:
Write `mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred)` that returns the average of the squared differences between true and predicted values.
Both lists have the same non-zero length.
hints: Compute the difference between each true and predicted pair.
`zip(y_true, y_pred)` lets you loop over both lists together.
Add up the squared differences and divide by the number of values.

title: Precision and recall
prompt:
Write `precision_recall(y_true, y_pred)` for binary labels (1 is the positive class) and return the tuple `(precision, recall)`.
precision = TP / (TP + FP) and recall = TP / (TP + FN). When a denominator is 0, that value is `0.0`.
hints: Loop over the pairs and count true positives (true 1, predicted 1), false positives (true 0, predicted 1) and false negatives (true 1, predicted 0).
precision = TP / (TP + FP) and recall = TP / (TP + FN).
Guard against dividing by zero: if a denominator is 0, return 0.0 for that value.

title: Cosine similarity

Embeddings are compared by the angle between their vectors. Write `cosine_similarity(a, b)` = dot(a, b) / (|a| * |b|).
Return `0.0` if either vector has length zero.

A vector's length is `math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in v))`.
